key_insight: Segment Anything Model 2 can produce transferable object-level embeddings (“object pointers”) during segmentation that capture tumour-relevant information, sometimes outperforming standard encoder features for prediction.
clinical_relevance: These results suggest a new way to reuse segmentation models for precision oncology tasks such as tumour type or recurrence prediction, especially when labelled data are limited.
method: Used SAM2 object pointers from the segmentation pathway as features instead of only encoder outputs.
Added a task-guided variant that jointly optimizes object pointers for segmentation plus downstream tumour prediction.
Compared against conventional encoder transfer and radiomics on two PET/CT tumour prediction tasks.
evidence_signal: Across two PET/CT evaluation tasks, task-guided pointers improved cancer-type classification, while segmentation-only pointers performed best for recurrence prediction.
watch_item: The approach still needs broader validation across larger, diverse datasets and clinical settings before it can be considered robust for deployment.
paper_title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models
